Provider semantics
  • Forward addresses and reverse coordinates use distinct inputs. Reverse coordinates are latitude,longitude; GeoJSON coordinates are longitude,latitude.
    • 

  • HTTP 200 can contain zero candidates. No result is selected automatically.
  • Provider quota exhaustion (402) is represented by the original upstream error contract. It is separate from the merchant's payment challenge.
    • 

  • Subscription responses may omit rate information. Returned licenses and native fields remain in customer deliveries.

Change compares adjacent retained UTC days in this range. Today and a session’s first observed day may have partial coverage. Missing days do not imply zero traffic. Starts and finishes belong to their own event dates; daily totals have no in-flight balance.

Retained sessions

Active sessions are checkpointing. Finalized sessions have an explicit final checkpoint. Interrupted sessions have no final checkpoint; their latest requests may be absent. The saved in-flight count is historical and does not describe current requests.

What these numbers mean

One request is one HTTP attempt, not one buyer. A 2xx response means the server finished writing; it does not prove on-chain settlement or client receipt.

Latency includes time until completion or disconnect. The p95 value is a histogram upper bound, not an exact percentile.

The live view and recent outcomes start fresh each session. When history is enabled, aggregate daily usage survives restarts in the seller’s private history folder. Individual request outcomes are never saved there.

Select the JSON record from your backend lookup, including status, headers and exactly one of body or bodyBase64. Maximum file size: 2 MiB. The existing binding validates the response before saving it.

How this affects paid requests

This ledger protects the merchant backend operation. A saved result can be replayed by the original handler; allowing a later request changes only the operation's eligibility to run. This console makes no backend request, issues no ticket and does not retry, verify or settle a payment. Each separately approved paid request still follows the original payment path.
